votes.root_cause:
_steady_size() in game/ui/rear_warning.gd multiplies base_px x size x heavy_scale and then clamps the product to the reserved corner's short side (216 px at 1080p). burst_rect() clamps again after the pulse scale. The grunt and heavy sizes are clamped independently, so once base x size x heavy_scale exceeds 216 (size above 1.04) the heavy stops growing, and above 1.35 the grunt reaches 216 too. The heavy_scale ratio is lost and the slider's upper range does nothing. The tuning range (rear_warning_size up to 3.0 in game/autoload/tuning_data.gd) is wider than anything that fits the corner. The same independent clamp in burst_rect() also cuts the heavy pop at the default (216 vs the grunt's 200, ratio 1.08).

A fix needs care. Capping the grunt at edge / heavy_scale and drawing the heavy as grunt x heavy_scale keeps the steady-state ratio. The pop frames need the same treatment (clamp the pulse scale per burst, or cap the grunt so that steady x (1 + pulse_grow) x heavy_scale fits). A strict cap would shrink the approved default, because 216 / (1.3 x 1.25) is about 133 px against 160 px. The cheaper route is to cap the slider range to what fits (about 1.04 at the defaults) and accept the clipped pop.

votes.root_cause:
`RearWarning._steady_size()` applies `rear_warning_heavy_scale` and then clamps to `0.2 * min(w,h)` (the plan-bound 20% x 20% corner, 216 px at 1080p). Heavy and grunt therefore saturate at different sizes and the ratio collapses to 1.0 (heavy hits 216 at size 1.04, grunt at 1.35). `burst_rect()` clamps again after `pulse_scale`, so the heavy pop is clipped even at default (216 against the grunt's 200).

The suggested fix is correct in direction. Cap the pre-heavy size at `edge / heavy_scale`, and draw a heavy burst as capped grunt x heavy_scale. That keeps heavy larger and inside the corner at every size. It has three limits, so don't oversell it.

- It does not revive the slider. Above about 1.04 the grunt is stuck at about 166 px and the heavy at 216 px. A dead upper slider range is inherent to the plan's binding clamp (M3-plan.md:166, ARCHITECTURE.md:540, "whatever rear_warning_size says"). Only the ratio can be preserved.
- The pop clip at default remains. Fixing it would mean capping steady x (1 + pulse_grow) to the corner, i.e. heavy <= 173 px. That changes the defaults the P1-hud call chose, so leave it, or make it a default-style call.
- The alternative of limiting the slider's `@export_range` is brittle. The ceiling depends on `rear_warning_base_px` (40-400) and `rear_warning_heavy_scale` (1-3) as well as the size slider.

Mind the edge case when heavy_scale is 1.0 (the slider minimum): heavy > grunt can't hold there.
